FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 27 April 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Small Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard has been prepared based on the prevalent practices in Indian industry and develop- 
ments at international level. In the preparation of this standard , considerable assistance has been 
derived from DIN 8376 : 1981 Subland twist drills with parallel shank for clearance holei and 
counterbores for hexagon socket head cap screws and slotted cheese head screws issued by the 
Deustches Institut fur Normung ( DIN ). 

The other Indian Standards in this series are: 

IS 12687 : 1989 Small tools — Subland drills with morse taper shanks for countersunk holes 
prior to tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12688 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shanks for clearance holes 
and countersinks for countersunk head screws prior to tapping screws thread 
— Specification 

IS 12690 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shanks for clearance holes 
and counterbores for slotted cheese head metric screws — Specification 

IS 12691 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shanks for holes prior to 
tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12692 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shanks for clearance holes and 
countersinks for countersunk head screws ~ Specification

SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

I'l This Indian Standard covers dimensions and 
other requirements for the subland twist drills 
with parallel shanks for producing clearance holes 
and counterbores for cheese head screws M3 
to M 10 — medium series conforming to IS 3406 
( Part 2 ) : 1986 'Dimensions for countersinks 
and counterbores : Part 2 Counterbores ( second 
revision )\

( Part 2 )

sion )

for twist drills (first

of twist drills 



3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard the defini- 
tions given in IS 10915 : 1984 shall apply. 

4 DIMENSIONS 

4.1 Dimensions of subland twist drill shall be as 
given in Table 1 . 

4.2 Tolerances 

Tolerance on the flute length /j and overall length 
/shall be ±5 mm. 

5 MATERIAL 

5*1 Material of subland twist drill shall be as 
given in IS 5099 ; 1983. 

6 HARDNESS 

6.1 Hardness of subland twist drill shall be as 
given in IS 5099 : 1983. 



7 GENERAL RBQjUIREMENTS 

7.1 Tool type 'N', right hand cutting will be 
supplied, unless otherwise specified. 

7.2 Diameter d and di shall be measured as near 
to the point as applicable. 

7.3 While using this drill, cutting speed should 
be selected according to the large diameter \r 
and the feed rate according to small diameter 
( pilot ) di. 

7.4 For the requirements not covered in this 
standard, the twist drill shall conform to the 
requirements as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

8 PROTECTIVE COATING 

8.1 Protective coating on subland twist drill shall 
be as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

9 SAMPLING 

9.1 The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall 
be in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 



shall be tested as given 



10 TESTS 

10.1 Subland twist drill 
in IS 5099: 1983. 

11 DESIGNATION 

11.1 A subland twist drill with parallel shanks of 
body diameter d = \0 mm and step diameter 
rfi=5*5 mm Tool Type N for right hand cutting 
and made of high speed steel conforming to this 
standard shall be designated as: 

Subland Twist Drill 10 x 55 IS 12689 

11.2 When required with tool type other than 
'N*, *H' or 'S' should be added in the designation 
after the diameter as appropriate. 

12 MARKING 

12.1 Subland twist drill shall be marked ah given 
in IS 5099 : 1983. 

13 PACKAGING 

13.1 Subland twist drill shall be packed as uivcn 
in IS 5099 : 1983.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys, the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection. 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
-liarmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these Publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This docs not preclude the free use. in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
urade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards arc reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, 
arc issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession 
of the latest amendments or edition Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving 
the following reference :
